title: Graphs: Reading and Interpreting Global Graphs
seo_title: Grade 7 Graphs Worksheets with Answers (CAPS Maths)
standard_text: Analyse and interpret global graphs of problem situations, with special focus on trends and features: linear or non-linear, constant, increasing or decreasing, maximum or minimum, discrete or continuous; draw global graphs from given descriptions of a problem situation.
meta_desc: Free CAPS Grade 7 graphs worksheets: conversion graphs, distance-time graphs, cost graphs and interpreting trends. 100 questions with memos.
key_big: Read the axes and the scale first.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Read the labels on both axes first.
  • Find what each small square is worth on the scale.
  • A line going up shows an increase; a line going down shows a decrease; a flat line shows no change.
  • On a distance-time graph, a steeper line means a higher speed.

Examples

Example

A flat part on a distance-time graph

distance does not change

Answer: the person stopped

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
The wrong axisRead the labels first.
The scaleWork out each square.
Flat means fastFlat means not moving.

Point P shows one term of the pattern as (term number, term value). What are its coordinates?
items.e: Go across first, then up. P is 3 across and 7 up, so it is (3; 7). (7; 3) gives the numbers in the wrong order: the term number comes first.

items.q: What is the value of term 4?
items.e: Find 4 on the term number axis and go up to the point. Read across: 9. 4 is the term number. 11 is term 5.

items.q: Liam graphs this pattern. Which point should he plot for term 3?
items.e: Each column is one point (term number, term value). Term 3 has value 10, so plot (3; 10). (10; 3) puts the term value first.

items.q: The pattern continues. Which point comes next?
items.e: The next term number is 6. The values go up by 2, so 11 + 2 = 13. The point is (6; 13). (13; 6) swaps the numbers.

items.q: What is the constant rate of this pattern?
items.e: Each step right (one more term), the points go up 2: 3, 5, 7, 9, 11. The constant rate is 2. 1 is the step in the term number. 3 is the value of term 1.

items.q: Which expression gives the term value for term number n?
items.e: The constant rate is 2, so start with 2n. 2 × 1 = 2 and term 1 is 3, so add 1: 2n + 1. 3n works for term 1 only.

items.q: A pattern has the term values 2, 5, 8 for terms 1, 2, 3. Which graph shows it?
items.e: The points are (1; 2), (2; 5), (3; 8): Graph C. Graph A plots (term value, term number). Graph B goes up by 2 and Graph D goes up by 1, but this pattern goes up by 3.

items.q: Which graph shows t = n + 5 for terms 1, 2 and 3?
items.e: 1 + 5 = 6, 2 + 5 = 7, 3 + 5 = 8. The points are (1; 6), (2; 7), (3; 8): Graph B. Graph A adds 4. Graph C swaps the numbers. Graph D goes down, but n + 5 grows.

items.q: Which graph shows t = 9 − 2n for terms 1, 2 and 3?
items.e: 9 − 2 = 7, 9 − 4 = 5, 9 − 6 = 3. The points are (1; 7), (2; 5), (3; 3): Graph D. Graph A goes down by 1, not 2. Graph B swaps the numbers. Graph C grows instead of shrinking.

items.q: What is the initial value of this pattern?
items.e: The initial value is the term value for term 0. The first point is on the vertical axis at 10, so the initial value is 10. Read the scale: each grid line is 5. 15 is term 1.

items.q: What are the coordinates of point P?
items.e: Go across first, then up. P is 3 across and 7 up, so it is (3; 7). (7; 3) gives the numbers in the wrong order: x comes first.

items.q: What is the value of y when x = 4?
items.e: Find 4 on the x-axis and go up to the point. Read across: y = 9. 4 is the value of x. 11 is the point for x = 5.

items.q: Liam plots this table on a graph. Which point should he plot?
items.e: Each column is one point (x, y). The column with 3 on top has 10 below, so plot (3; 10). (10; 3) plots (y, x).

items.q: To plot the point (2; 7), start at (0; 0). How do you move?
items.e: The first number tells how far across and the second tells how far up: 2 right, then 7 up. 7 right, then 2 up plots (7; 2).

items.q: The pattern continues. Which point comes next?
items.e: The next x is 6. y goes up by 2, so 11 + 2 = 13. The point is (6; 13). (13; 6) swaps the numbers: x comes first.

items.q: Which expression gives y for any x?
items.e: The points are (1; 3), (2; 5), (3; 7). y goes up by 2, so start with 2x. 2 × 1 = 2 and y is 3, so add 1: 2x + 1. 3x works for (1; 3) only.

items.q: A table of values has x = 1, 2, 3 and y = 3, 5, 7. Which graph shows these points?
items.e: The points are (1; 3), (2; 5), (3; 7). Graph B shows them. Graph A plots (y, x). Graph C adds 1 each time and Graph D is 2x without the + 1.

items.q: How does y change each time x goes up by 1?
items.e: The points are (0; 12), (1; 10), (2; 8). Each step right, y drops 2: y goes down by 2.

items.q: Which expression gives y for any x?
items.e: When x = 0, y = 12, and y goes down by 2 each time: 12 − 2x. 10 − 2x uses the point for x = 1 as the start.

items.q: Which graph shows y = x + 4 for x = 1, 2, 3?
items.e: 1 + 4 = 5, 2 + 4 = 6, 3 + 4 = 7. The points are (1; 5), (2; 6), (3; 7): Graph D. Graph A plots (y, x). Graph B adds 3. Graph C goes down, but x + 4 goes up.

items.q: On a distance-time graph, what does a horizontal (flat) line show?
items.e: Distance does not change, so the person is not moving.

items.q: On a distance-time graph, what does a steeper line show?
items.e: More distance in the same time means a faster speed.

items.q: On a distance-time graph (distance from home), what does a line sloping down show?
items.e: The distance from home is getting smaller: travelling back towards home.

items.q: What does the gradient of a distance-time graph represent?
items.e: Gradient = distance ÷ time = speed.

items.q: A distance-time graph goes up 30 km in 2 hours. What is the speed?
A distance-time graph goes up 12 km in 30 minutes. What is the speed?
items.e: 30 minutes = 0,5 hours. 12 ÷ 0,5 = 24 km/h.

items.q: A cyclist rides 20 km in 1 hour, stops for 30 minutes, then rides 10 km in 30 minutes. Which part is fastest?
c: Both riding parts are the same speed
items.e: First: 20 km/h. Last: 10 ÷ 0,5 = 20 km/h. Both riding parts are the same speed.

items.q: Why can a distance-time graph never go straight up (vertical)?
c: It can, if you are fast
Because the axes are the wrong way round
That would mean moving a distance in no time
items.e: A vertical line means distance changes with zero time passing: moving a distance in no time, which is impossible.

items.q: Two walkers' graphs cross. What does the crossing point show?
c: They are at the same place at the same time
items.e: Same distance and same time: they are at the same place at the same time.

items.q: A graph of a car's journey is a curve that gets steeper. What is the car doing?
items.e: The gradient (speed) is increasing: speeding up.
